Hi Elena / Vanessa — following up from Legal/Security. I completed a targeted assessment for LogisticsCloud with the InfoSec team. Summary below (high level):

- Data scope: LogisticsCloud will receive pseudonymized delivery records (tracking_id, status_ts, carrier_code). No account passwords, payment card data, or national IDs.
- Controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, role-based access control, quarterly access reviews, and a 72-hour breach notification SLA to processors.
- Compliance evidence: LogisticsCloud provided a current SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 certificate. We will provide the SOC 2 redacted snapshot via secure link once we confirm recipients.
- DPIA: We ran Redwood's lightweight DP assessment specific to onward transfer and concluded residual risk is low with the above controls and contractual guardrails (SCCs locked in). Full DPIA attached: redwood_subprocessor_assessment_LogisticsCloud.pdf

Regarding consent & onward transfers: under Redwood's DPA and the EU SCCs, this type of operational subprocessor addition is covered by the existing contractual framework, provided we notify customers 30 days in advance and maintain the documented assessment. If EuroBank requires explicit customer approval (DocuSign signature) for their Annex A, we can sign the amendment. We recommend you select one of the following options:

1) Consent by notice: Redwood provides notice and the assessment; EuroBank publishes LogisticsCloud in Annex A after a 30-day review period.
2) Explicit consent: sign a short amendment via DocuSign authorizing this onboarding now (we can fast-track).

We have prepared a current subprocessor roster CSV (redwood_subprocessor_roster_Q3_2025.csv) and a redacted SOC 2 excerpt; I'm attaching the assessment PDF now.

If EuroBank wants to expedite, send the DocuSign envelope link and we'll countersign. Our legal contact for signatures is legal-approvals@redwood.com.
